title: N=16 packed NF4 block_k=128 versus block_k=256 screening
environment: Conda env ai; torch 2.11.0+cu128; Triton 3.6.0; bitsandbytes 0.50.0
result: K128 lowers register use and raises theoretical occupancy, but is slower for M=2 in both projections; not integrated into runtime.
shape_invariance: For both schedules and both projections, M=1 and M=2 outputs were bitwise equal row-by-row to separate calls of that same schedule on each singleton row.
limits: The CUDA-event sample has five rounds per M and projection; q_proj M=1 had two warm-up/clock outliers, so its near-parity median should not be read as a stable speedup.
Nsight durations are single profiled launches, not benchmark latencies.
K128 changes the arithmetic/reduction chunk schedule and would require a separate B1 reference contract if pursued further.
These operator probes do not establish whole-model token or KV equivalence under K128.
